answer.rationale: The competitor's price cut creates urgency, but memory_73 explicitly warns against generalizing targeted discounting as sustainable—the acquired cohort in that experiment failed to survive first renewal. Instead, deploy activation_messaging (memory_91 shows week-one engagement lift) combined with simplified onboarding (memory_86, memory_31 confirm durable adoption gains) to improve product stickiness and perceived value for at-risk SMB accounts. This addresses churn defensively without sacrificing long-term cohort quality. Enterprise sales assist (memory_44) is valuable but slower and doesn't address the immediate SMB churn wave. Referral incentives (memory_57) work on established customers, not those actively reconsidering. A standard_experiment targeting churning SMB cohorts with faster activation and better onboarding friction removal preserves the strategic constraint: sustainable qualified revenue, not unsustainable discounting that degrades cohort economics.
